title: Serving Runtime API Stability Checklist (v0 -> v1)
body:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact, operationally-focused checklist for moving the serving runtime API from the informal v0 surface we currently accept to a stable v1. The goal is not a full spec (that will live in the repo), but a pragmatic set of compatibility guarantees, error-code taxonomy, and migration tasks that engineers, SDK authors, and SREs can act on.

Context & constraints:
- Runtime must support existing hosted and dedicated customers with minimal client changes.
- We cannot add breaking defaults that change request semantics (e.g., default model switching, aggressive truncation) without opt-in.
- Kernel scheduling and KV cache hints are evolving; the API must allow graceful rollout of improved kernels and cache behaviors without breaking clients.

Audience:
- Serving runtime engineers, SDK maintainers, integrators, QA, and SRE oncall.

Quick guarantees to offer in v1 (short form):
1) Stable parsing: any well-formed JSON request that satisfied v0 fields continues to be accepted and processed with the same semantics unless the client opts into a new envelope version.
2) Additive fields: server may add new optional fields to responses or new optional request keys; clients must ignore unknown fields.
3) Semantic versioning of the request envelope: we will advance the request_envelope.version only on explicitly breaking changes. Minor/patch updates won't change version.
4) Error codes: introduce stable, machine-parseable error codes with mapped HTTP statuses; text messages are advisory only.
5) Negotiation: clients may declare capability vectors; servers must honor compatibility where possible or fail with a specific compatibility error that contains a migration hint.

Proposed minimal request envelope (informal example):
{
  "request_id": "<uuid>",        # opaque id for tracing
  "client_version": "sdk-python-0.12.3",
  "request_envelope": {
    "version": "0.1",             # bump to 1.0 only for breaking changes
    "model": "redwood/guanaco-13b",
    "input": "...",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "temperature": 0.0,
    "kv_cache_hint": {
      "prefetch": false,
      "expected_prefix_len": 128
    },
    "scheduling": {
      "priority": "normal",        # normal | high | low
      "batching": "auto"           # auto | manual | disabled
    },
    "fallback_policy": "region-first"   # optional string enum
  }
}

Notes on fields:
- request_envelope.version: string; servers must treat missing version as legacy-0. Minor version strings like 0.1, 0.2 indicate non-breaking evolution.
- client_version: freeform; used for telemetry and targeted rollout.
- kv_cache_hint: advisory only. Servers may ignore or reinterpret these hints. If a hint is materially incompatible (e.g., client expects persistent KV but server is stateless), return COMPAT_INCOMPATIBLE_CLIENT_HINT.
- scheduling.batch: affects how request enters batching queues; adding new scheduling attributes must be optional and additive.

Error code taxonomy (stable codes, machine-friendly):
- ERR_INVALID_SCHEMA -> HTTP 400: request JSON is malformed or required v0 fields are missing.
- ERR_AUTH -> HTTP 401/403: authentication/authorization errors.
- ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND -> HTTP 404: requested model or pinned version unavailable.
- ERR_KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED -> HTTP 422: model requested requires a kernel not present on node pool. Contains "supported_kernels" hint in metadata.
- ERR_KV_MISS -> HTTP 409: a cache-dependent request failed due to KV absence; includes recovery hint (retry without prefix).
- ERR_BACKPRESSURE -> HTTP 429: server is applying backpressure; response MAY include "retry_after_ms" and "suggested_fallback".
- ERR_INCOMPATIBLE_CLIENT -> HTTP 426: client needs upgrade (contains migrations).
- ERR_INTERNAL -> HTTP 500: unexpected server error; include trace id.

Design rules for errors:
- Errors always include: code (one of stable tokens above), message (human), trace_id, and optional details array of short strings.
- Servers may include mitigation_hint as a single short string (up to 200 chars).
- Do NOT rely on error message strings for programmatic logic; use code.

Compatibility guarantees (detailed):
- Additive safety: adding optional keys to request or response is safe. Clients must ignore unknown keys.
- Default stability: changing the default value of an existing request key is a breaking change; must either be gated behind a new request_envelope.version or be announced + opt-in via client_version.
- Field removal: removing a field is breaking. Deprecate for at least 3 months with server-side compatibility: accept the old field but ignore it, logged at debug.
- Semantic sharpening: tightening semantics (e.g., making temperature negative disallowed) must produce ERR_INVALID_SCHEMA for clients sending older values and be announced as a breaking version.

Negotiation and rollout primitives:
- client_capabilities (proposed): clients can provide a capability vector like: ["kv-persistent", "scheduling-batching-v2"]. Servers may return the subset they support in the response metadata.
- server_advertised_capabilities endpoint: a light endpoint for SDKs to fetch supported capabilities for a region/model pair. This can be cached.

KV cache behavior and compat notes:
- KV hints are advisory. Do not expose persistence guarantees in v0 -> v1 unless we can back them with audit/logging and SLA.
- If server offers persistent-kv for an enterprise deployment, require explicit opt-in field: "kv_persistence: { mode: "enabled", tenancy: "dedicated" }". This is breaking and should be part of v1 stable offering for Dedicated/Private customers only.

Scheduler/kernel negotiation patterns:
- Requests may include "preferred_kernels": ["fast-attn-v3", "matmul-fp16"] (optional). Server will try the first available kernel; if none available, respond with ERR_KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED with suggestions.
- Do not require clients to know kernel names in the general hosted API; make preferred_kernels an advanced opt-in.

Migration checklist (developer & release):
- [ ] Add structured error code header to all runtime responses (code, trace_id, details).
- [ ] Ensure all existing endpoints accept unknown optional fields without 400s. Run fuzz tests across SDKs.
- [ ] Implement server-side request_envelope.version parsing and default legacy behavior.
- [ ] Add small compatibility test-suite that runs on PRs: send v0 clients with representative payloads and ensure identical behavior (within epsilon) on staging.
- [ ] Publish SDK migration guide (breaking changes section) and example patches for Python/TS clients.
- [ ] Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic), regional ramp, global. Block on key metrics: error rate stable, p95 latency not increased >10%.

Operational guidance for SRE / oncall:
- If ERR_BACKPRESSURE rises above 0.5% of requests in a region for >10 minutes, escalate to scheduler owners; automatically enable soft-fallback policy (route to lower-cost variant) for non-enterprise traffic.
- Track ERR_KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED frequency when releasing new kernels; label telemetry by model and pool.

SDK author checklist:
- Respect unknown response fields.
- Surface machine-friendly error.code and trace_id to integrators; do not place them only in logs.
- Default to sending client_version on all requests.
- Provide an easy opt-in toggle for advanced fields (preferred_kernels, kv_cache_hint).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize a stable metadata envelope for all responses vs. embedding into body? (impact: CDNs / caching behavior).
- How to surface KV persistence SLAs to customers in the product catalog without leaking implementation?
- Decide canonical format for capability vectors (strings vs. structured).

Appendix: example error response (suggested canonical shape)
{
  "code": "ERR_BACKPRESSURE",
  "message": "region overloaded, applying queueing",
  "trace_id": "0f47aa2e-...",
  "retry_after_ms": "250",
  "details": ["consider lowering max_tokens", "suggested_fallback: model-smaller-1"]
}

Contact & next steps:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- Reach out: #eng-runtime on Slack for design reviews.
- Next milestone: convert this checklist into a formal spec doc and add examples in the runtime repo (milestone: runtime-api-v1-spec, target: 2024-12-15).

Footer: this is a working draft: expect edits, TODOs sprinkled inline, and follow-ups after the first canary run.
